title: Elevated-Temperature Tribo-Corrosion Response of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: An as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy of the AlCoCrFeNi family (often AlCoCrFeNi2.1), featuring a fine lamellar B2 (Al-, Ni-, Co-rich) + FCC (Cr-, Fe-rich) microstructure.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion tests using a reciprocating tribometer integrated with electrochemical control in 3.5 wt% NaCl at 25°C vs ~80°C (some tests at open-circuit and under potentiostatic polarization), measuring friction, wear volume (mm^3/N·m), and corrosion current during sliding.
recollection.structure: Guess: Formation of a compact tribo-oxide glaze at elevated temperature composed of Cr- and Al-rich oxides with spinel-type (Ni,Co,Fe) oxides; subsurface severe plastic deformation and selective dissolution/oxidation of the Al-rich B2 lamellae, yielding ridge–valley relief aligned with the eutectic lamellae.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Elevated temperature accelerates both corrosion and repassivation; under sliding, rapid tribo-oxidation builds a protective oxide glaze that lowers friction and stabilizes the contact. The Al-rich B2 phase preferentially dissolves/oxidizes, while Cr enriches the surface, promoting a more protective film. Net material loss is governed by wear–corrosion synergy that shifts from more corrosion-influenced at room temperature to tribo-oxide–controlled at elevated temperature.
recollection.results: Guess: Coefficient of friction drops from ~0.55±0.05 at 25°C to ~0.40±0.05 at ~80°C due to tribo-oxide formation; wear rate decreases from ~6×10^-5 to ~3×10^-5 mm^3/N·m. Corrosion current density during sliding increases with temperature (e.g., ~3 µA/cm^2 at 25°C to ~15 µA/cm^2 at 80°C), but the protective tribo-oxide reduces the synergy component, with the synergy fraction declining from ~40% to ~25% of total material loss. EIS/ECM indicators show reduced charge-transfer resistance at higher T (e.g., ~20 to ~5 kΩ·cm^2) alongside a slight noble shift of OCP (~+50 mV) after tribo-oxide stabilization.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies reciprocating elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion and broadly notes competition between oxidation/repassivation and sliding. However, it gives incorrect test temperatures and unsupported electrolyte/potentiostatic details, invents selective B2 dissolution and a consistently protective oxide glaze, and misses the retained L12/B2 structure, the 50 °C wear minimum, and disruption at 100 °C. All reported friction, wear, electrochemical, and synergy numbers are inconsistent with the actual results.
